answer: Reputation-weighted rate ceilings: each identity's transaction throughput is capped by its long-run accuracy, so clones start at a ledge of near-zero capacity while a steady honest pulse earns expanded limits. Every new identity must fund a slow warm-up of real settled trades before it can move meaningful value, and duplicate accounts each pay that same ramp cost separately. A sybil cluster therefore spends N times the juniper of one honest operator — capital, latency, and failed-trade risk — to match a single trusted account's throughput, making cloning strictly more expensive.
